keyQuestions.text: Q1: Where is overlay-engine.cjs (status/apply/capture/repin/rollback) incorrect or unsafe against its own docs and tests, for example manifest drift, protectedPaths and repin.exclude handling, the not-copied list, partial failure and rollback?
Q2: Which /doctor command messages, prompts and outputs confuse an external-repo user or leave them without a next step (overlay, install, symlink, setup, helper)?
Q3: What onboarding friction does a brand-new external repository hit when linking or copying Skilled in, from INSTALL-SKILLED.md through /doctor:install, /doctor:symlink and /doctor:setup?
Q4: How safe is upgrading or re-pinning a copied Skilled tree, and what would make re-pin, the overlay-guard hook and rollback safer or easier to recover from?
Q5: Where do INSTALL-SKILLED.md, overlays.md, the doctor command docs and the skill README disagree with the code, and which improvements rank highest by user impact?

keyFindings.text: f-iter001-001 (P1) — `.env`-prefix heuristic permanently blocks legitimate template files
f-iter001-002 (P2) — A re-pin refuses when an upstream-deleted file is already missing locally
f-iter001-003 (P2) — The not-copied list silently drops upstream additions at top-level paths the tree does not hold
f-iter001-004 (P2) — Not-copied findings are ephemeral; `status` never re-surfaces them
f-iter001-005 (P2) — An interrupted re-pin leaves no durable run status and no discoverable rollback pointer
f-iter001-006 (P3) — The not-copied summary appends AGENTS.md guidance to unrelated paths
f-iter003-001 (P1) — `status` never checks `pin.commit` against the bytes in the tree
f-iter003-002 (P1) — A wrong `pin.commit` corrupts the re-pin drift base
f-iter003-003 (P2) — `in-sync` is decided before the pin, so a fully green status can coexist with a wrong pin
f-iter003-004 (P3) — `remove-root` bypasses the state machine, so a re-created file is always "overlay-edited"
f-iter004-001 (P1) — Rollback restores bytes without comparing them to the current tree
f-iter004-002 (P1) — The guard stops protecting exactly when the tree is damaged
f-iter004-003 (P2) — A green stage is not a rehearsal of the live run
f-iter004-004 (P2) — The guard is a tool-call guard, not a write boundary, and it spawns the engine once per path
f-iter004-005 (P3) — Successful re-pin runs are never pruned, and no command lists them
f-iter004-006 (P3) — Runtime coverage is documented only in the hook README, and `/doctor:overlay` never mentions the guard
